utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we have the witness, there is a decision we would like to announce. At the end of the trial session yesterday, the Defence counsel for Mr. Naletilic and Mr. Martinovic jointly requested that OTP witness testimony of Mr. Marko Prelec, who is scheduled to testify today, December 6, is postponed until after Christmas recess. This morning, the Chamber has received the written joint objections of the Defence. The Defence argues that they have not had sufficient time to study and examine the transcript that shall be submitted to the Chamber with the witness. As the Defence counsel themselves stated in their written objections, the witness is only called to lay a foundation for the introduction of the transcripts of taped meetings from the Office of the President of the Republic of Croatia. That witness has already testified before this Chamber in this case, with regard to the introduction of other Prosecution exhibits. His testimony on 25 and 26 October, 2001, clearly shows that Mr. Prelec is a witness who can and will only testify as to the way he has selected and obtained documents for the Prosecutor's Office and how those documents were processed within the Prosecutor's Office. The Trial Chamber finds, therefore, that the witness is not in a position to testify with regard to the substance of the specific contents of the transcripts. Therefore, the Defence counsel is not prejudiced in any way by hearing the testimony of Mr. Prelec today. In particular, the Defence will be granted due time to file their written response to the application of the Prosecution to have the presidential transcripts admitted into evidence. This has been the practice before this Trial Chamber throughout the case and it will apply also with regard to the collection of the presidential transcripts. For these reasons, the Trial Chamber rejects the objections of the Defence counsel. The Prosecution may call their witness as scheduled. It is so decided. Yes, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. It is not related to this issue, but I have one procedural matter to address, and of course it is nothing to do with this ruling. We have understood this ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, about ten days ago, when Witnesses OO and QQ were deposed, I think that there were two situations that were not completely cleared up. During the evidence of Witness OO, it was said that he would write -- that he would give a written statement about the wooden rifle and the museum in which it is now located. We have so far not been informed on whether the witness has indeed submitted this written statement, whether it has been submitted to the Court, and whether the Defence will be given access to it. So this is the first issue that has not been fully clarified for the Defence. And the second situation was with the Witness QQ, who asserted that certain pressures were exerted upon him and, again, it was agreed that he would put it down in writing for the Trial Chamber. We do not know whether this has been done and whether we, as the Defence, will have an opportunity to review this statement. We would therefore like the Trial Chamber to give us their position on these two issues. In relation to that, we would like to point out that our clients have serious objections to parts of the evidence given by these two witnesses, because in part of their testimony, they were surprise witnesses, giving evidence that has never surfaced before. One of them was -- one had to do with a member of the ABiH, and the other one was contact with a prison inmate. This raises certain concerns to the Defence and we therefore would like to see what the -- what the position of the Trial Chamber is in regards of these witnesses, OO and QQ. It is important for us at this stage of the proceedings because we need to know whether, in our own case, we need to look to bring some new witnesses that would be able to counter what these witnesses have said, and we should be able to know this at this time because we are in the process of preparing our pre-defence conference. So this would be an important point for us to have resolved as soon as possible. It does not have to be obviously right now but it was time for us to bring it up now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as for the two statements from Witness OO and QQ, this Trial Chamber has made an oral order to the Prosecutor that asks for those statements and also asks for the wooden rifles. We are expecting some response from the side of the Prosecution about those issues. As for the surprise witness, in this case, we also need the explanation from the side of the Prosecution. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, as to the statements of OO and QQ, and the wooden rifles, the wooden rifle situation, I'm happy to report, perhaps coincidentally or what have you, we anticipate providing those materials today, sometime in the course of today's session. So that should be done. We weren't going to start today doing that, but sometime between now and 7.00 we would hope to present that material to the Chamber and to the Defence. As to the surprise witness that, I have to admit, off the top of my head, I'm not sure what's being referenced there. Mr. President, if you or Defence can assist me, I'm not sure what that's about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we are not going to discuss about this matter in this courtroom. I hope that both parties could meet after today's sitting to clarify this issue and report to this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, good afternoon. Yesterday when the Trial Chamber decided to take under advisement the Defence motion which has been ruled on today, and we understand that ruling and we obviously will abide by that ruling, it was asked by the Trial Chamber if Witness XX would be available to testify today, and I believe my learned colleague Mr. Bos, particularly, had indicated yes, he would be available to testify today. So just as a matter of curiosity, since Mr. Prelec is an OTP witness, will he be bringing -- will he be testifying tomorrow and XX today? That's my only question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we believe that the ruling we made just now is quite clear, that is, the Prosecution may call their witnesses as scheduled. Mr. Scott, do you want to add something?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, in consultation with Mr. Bos, who will be handling that next -- not Mr. Prelec, but the next witness, in fact, we're largely neutral but, in fact, it may be just as well to take Mr. Bos's witness next because that will then, of course, be -- give us greater assurance that he will finish before the end of the week and can return home. If we took -- of course, if we took Mr. Prelec today and depending on developments, it could be that the next witness would not finish by 1.00 tomorrow and we would have the unfortunate situation where the witness would have to stay over the weekend, so it may be the way things have evolved in the course of the week that it's just as well, and Mr. Bos says -- tells me he is prepared, with my thanks, that we go ahead and take the next witness after this, and then take Mr. Prelec following that. And since, indeed, he is here in The Hague, we have a bit more flexibility, if that's acceptable to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will hear the witness according to the order you suggested.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Usher, would you please bring the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Please sit down. Please remember that you are still under the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. President, good afternoon, Your Honours. Mr. President, I do not have many questions, but because of the nature of the questions that I'm going to ask now, I'm going to request a private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Mr. President, closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek, cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, Your Honours, I was not quick enough. I would have asked you to stay in closed session for -- I only have a few questions, but I think it's appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go back to the closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to ask you just a very few questions. As there was considerable examination about the identification of the accused Vinko Martinovic, or the cross-examination, so let me ask you a few questions about that. The men who came to your apartment first on the 9th of May and then again on the 13th of June, did you know any of those four men just from living in Mostar or having lived there for some time, did you know them or know of them before seeing them on those two days?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We're sorry, we cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, for some reason we're not getting , I think, the broadcast.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, your microphone is not on either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, can you try again?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I see Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I heard the question, so do you want the Prosecutor to ask his question again and then allow me to object to it or to object to it straight away, because the question is in the transcript? Well, I will make my objection, and then you can see from the transcript what it is about, namely, in that examination, the witness answered this question. So the witness, as it was repeated, is leading because both in direct and in cross-examination, the witness said that she saw Vinko Martinovic for the first time there and that she found out about him at the Heliodrom and that she had heard his last name before. So with this question, the Prosecutor is suggesting the answer to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, would you please skip this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I was trying to approach it in an orderly way, but I'll ask then if the usher could assist me by showing the B/C/S version of the witness's statement to the OTP on the 26th of September, 1998 in front of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, I put before you what we call a B/C/S version of the interview statement which you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor's representatives on the - I will double-check the date one more time - 26th of September, 1998. Now, directing your attention to the top of the page that's been marked. I don't want you to read that out loud but would you just read -- there's -- would you just read the top several lines, paragraph of that document, and then I will just have a question for you. Now let me just -- without looking -- have you had a chance to look at that, Witness WW? Witness, have you had a chance to look at it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, without looking back at the statement --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your microphone, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, without looking further back at the statement, does it refresh your recollection that you had told the OTP in September of 1998 that you recognise these four men because they had all lived in the Mostar area before this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And to follow up on that question, did you know anything, for instance, that Mr. Martinovic had done while he was employed or engaged in business before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I heard, Mr. Martinovic drove a taxi before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, Witness, you said yesterday in your testimony --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And it was in yesterday's transcript, it would have been page 3, Your Honour, but since the page numbers have changed since yesterday, I can't refer back, but -- my apology, my apology, page 68, line 21 yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, you said, "I know this Vinko Martinovic here." Now, based on what you saw on the 9th of May, 1993, and the 13th of June, 1993, Witness WW, do you believe you know, in fact, the Vinko Martinovic, Stela, who evicted you from your apartment, not once but twice? Do you know who that person is? I mean, had you seen him -- you saw him on those two occasions, and is that what you base your testimony on, or did you see him any time after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I would recognise Mr. Stela always and everywhere after all that, but because on both occasions I was the first to be evicted, that is on the 9th of May, and sent to the Heliodrom, and on the 13th of June, when I was sent to the other bank, I never saw him. That is, as of that date, the 13th of June, until now, I never saw him again, but Mr. Stela --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: But on both occasions, Mr. Stela was at my place. I mean, on both -- both times, he -- he did that. He did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, witness. Just to clarify, you had not seen him since that time. Now, one final question. About the door -- there was also extensive questioning about where you were at the door of your flat in relationship to the door of the building that you were living in --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It may assist -- sorry, Mr. President, I'm just thinking the easiest way to do this. I was considering having the witness do a sketch, but with your permission, I'll try to ask it first, if it will work this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, ma'am, that the door into the building, that is from the outside into your building itself, was immediately adjacent to the door into your flat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: The front door, that is the door into the building, to the staircase, there is about a metre or perhaps two, and then you climb a couple of steps, and there is my door. Perhaps five. I just can't remember. I mean, it's just right there. It's really very close by.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Standing at the door of your flat, could you also see the door into the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Once again, thank you, Witness. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions from judges? Judge Clark?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Madam Witness, can I ask you a few questions? When the men came to your flat on the evening of the 9th of May -- can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: On the 9th of May, and also on the 13th of June, you described how you were in the first flat, so you were the first to be pushed out. Were you mistreated or manhandled in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to begin with, they came in the morning, not in the evening. Secondly, when I came out, you know, like any woman, it was the beginning of my menopause, and when they came, my period started, so that I went back into the room, got some Tampax, put them in my handbag and because -- and this bag -- then my bag then looked rather small, and so when I came out in front -- when I came out and Mr. Stela was standing in front of the building, I don't know what he thought that I had in the bag, and he started for me to take the bag, and I, knowing that I had something in my handbag that nobody -- no man should see, I tried -- I clutched at this handbag, and at that time he started pushing me, trying to -- trying to prise my hands over and get this handbag, and then he pushed me and this handbag fell, and he kicked me. He kicked me so -- kicked me with his boot so that I felt it, and I was left speechless with a tremendous pain in my spine, but it is all over now. I mean, it was just a fleeting moment when that happened to me. I don't know. I don't know what he thought I had in this handbag. And believe me, I had nothing else except that thing which I personally needed. So I had to go without it. I went to the Heliodrom without anything, and I was in terrible trouble at the Heliodrom because they gave me nothing. And you know, a woman who has something like that ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Must have been ghastly for you. Another question I wanted to ask is that yesterday, I thought - and I wondered was it my imagination - I thought, and then I started to write the word and it didn't come back, that you mentioned something about a journalist being mistreated. Did you say that or was it my imagination?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did say that. I did. The journalist -- the gentleman who was with that gentleman, he grabbed him abruptly, but this gentleman here interceded so that he wasn't mishandled in any way, except he just grabbed him like this, but the gentleman here intervened and he stayed there. He stayed there in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Did this journalist live in your building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I wonder - it's an unusual request - can I go into, I don't know whether it's closed or private session. I want to mention two names. I'm not familiar with the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Certainly fine with the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: No objection whatsoever, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: My problem is I don't know whether it's closed session or private session. I don't want names to be revealed. What do I ask for? Private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think in this courtroom, because it's a rather unique situation, it's essentially the same as being in closed session because the -- it's closed session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's go to closed session anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. You stated that you knew Mr. Martinovic before the war, or you knew of him, and you said that he was a taxi driver. Yesterday when you were giving your evidence, you mentioned a coffee bar or a cafe bar which was associated with the Martinovic family. Now, my question is: Did Mr. Martinovic, Mr. Vinko Martinovic, own a coffee bar before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, believe me, but I know that the owner of that coffee bar which Mr. Martinovic used, that its original owner was a Mr. Garo Kovacevic. I know that because I would go past that coffee bar every day and he was a Serb, and I know that he was the owner of that coffee bar. Not only I, everybody in Mostar knew that he owned it because that coffee bar was in one of the elite part of the town. It was near the Velez stadium and there were new buildings, and across the street there was a new building, and that coffee bar was owned by Garo Kovacevic and later it was used by Stela.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Do you know who appears to exercise ownership over that coffee bar at the moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, believe me, I don't because I just don't go there anymore. I can't go there anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: When we hear people talking about Vinko Martinovic or Stela's coffee bar, it's not one that he owns, it's one that he frequents; is that what you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Mr. Martinovic, since Mr. Kovacevic, who was a Serb, left the town, Mr. Martinovic took over that coffee bar and worked in it, at the coffee bar, worked regularly, but who is there now, I do not know, because I haven't lived in that area for the last nine years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. The other thing I wanted to ask you is that you mentioned a few minutes ago that you were still on -- maybe we should be in closed session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Judge Diarra.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: Witness WW, I'd like to ask you, when the police turned up in front of your apartment in the morning, did -- they check your identity documents. Then that policeman said, "I'm sorry, I have to kick you out, otherwise they will kill me." And your husband, who I imagine is very brave, told him not to worry. He didn't ask him, "Who will kill you?"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, when this guy, and he was quite a young lad, when he entered my flat, I could see that he was upset, too, and because my husband and I were alone in the flat and he had no problem with us. He simply -- I suppose he was also scared of it that something could happen and that is when he said, "You have to go out, otherwise they'll kill me." So obviously he was afraid from somebody else because he was young, he was really young, and I suppose he didn't have very much experience. What he told me was, "They collected me from the Avenija and they put me in a uniform and ordered me to do this," and that is when my husband told him, "Don't worry, son, we shall come out without a problem, because on the 9th of May we've already had that kind of experience," and on the 13th of May - how to put it mildly - it was natural for me to come out without causing any trouble to those people because I think that this young man wasn't really quite ready for that kind of task, that kind of job, but there you are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you were shown the street -- when you were shown the plan to identify the street, you said that the names of the streets have changed, that you were not able to find your way around the map. How have these names of the streets changed, and have the street names been now changed back again to their old ones? Do you hope once you return to your apartment that that street will regain its old name? How did the street names change?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, the gentlemen changed the street names and called them after their important historical figures. The street which was called Kalimova and which all of us Mostarans know, including Mr. Stela, or Petra Drapsina, now it's called Queen Katarina, and other streets, but these are all the names which this, the current authority, gave those streets. I suppose that even if I go back to my old apartment, I don't think they will change the street name back to its old name again. I think it will remain as it is called now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, madam. And I'd like to congratulate you on the -- on your calm and on the serenity with which you answered all our questions despite the drama, in spite of what you experienced. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions as a result of the Judge's questions? Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do, Mr. President. A few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Madam, what you have answered to Her Honour Judge Clark that Vinko Martinovic tried to get your handbag, to snatch your handbag from you and he kicked you in the back, can you explain why is it that you never once mentioned it before in none of your statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, counsel, believe me, these are horrible moments and I, frankly speaking, tried to forget it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: When you said that this Martinovic's soldier started towards your neighbour to beat him or hit him or something and that Vinko Martinovic then intervened, do you mean that he protected him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when this gentleman came out of the door, really, he was very upset and he started for him and grabbed him. But this gentleman, yes, he really said, "Leave him alone." He did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You mean Mr. Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Martinovic. He really said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Yesterday - perhaps there was a misunderstanding and perhaps the transcript is not correct - but yesterday, speaking about this coffee bar at the old Velez stadium, that it was called Kovacevic's, but the transcript never says, and that is I did not understand you saying that Mr. Martinovic was the owner of that coffee bar ever.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, on the 16th of May, when I returned from the Heliodrom - and Mr. Stela knows that - when I returned, Mr. Stela was there. I mean, everybody in the town, everybody said that Mr. Stela was in Mr. Kovacevic's coffee bar, and every day when I started working, because I --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I had returned to work, I kept -- he was there all the time. I saw him there all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Not so much an objection, but if I might be allowed, I think what's a bit confusing about the evidence about the coffee bar is the word "ownership," because I think what the -- well, I don't know. I think that is the issue. I think she just says -- she does not say that Mr. Stela owned the coffee bar, and that's why she keeps going back to this Serb, but whether he was operating or had taken control -- I think it's the word "ownership," Your Honour, that's causing the confusion, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let Mr. Seric continue his question about this coffee bar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I will say to you, Vinko Martinovic says that he never owned - and let me finish - that he never owned or that he was never in that coffee bar, that he never ran it, that he never took it over, and if you remember, throughout that time, it was Stojicic, called Buli, who ran this coffee bar after Kovacevic all the time that he had rented it. What would you say to this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, it does not mean anything to me because I do not know Mr. Stojicic. Believe me, I do not know him. But Mr. Stela -- and it's not only me, but in Mostar, in the city of Mostar, it is common knowledge that Mr. Stela entered Mr. Kovacevic's coffee bar. Who ran it, who was the owner, I really don't know, but Mr. Stela, of course, can say what he knows, but I'm telling you what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: The name Mali Raj, Little Paradise, that was the name of the coffee bar; does it ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Well, that is the name of the coffee bar that the Martinovic family owns. So what you are telling me is it is simply the grapevine, it is the gossip which reached your ears; this is not what you're claiming?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying that I saw Mr. Stela - Mr. Stela - in front of the coffee bar, and that was almost on a daily basis, every day, as I would come -- return from work. And everybody in the town -- and I do not know whether it is his property or not, and as far as I'm concerned, it does not really matter. But I do know that throughout this time, most Mostar talked about Mr. Stela taking over Mr. Kovacevic's coffee bar after he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Vinko Martinovic run this coffee bar, that he collected the bills, that he had some people under him who ran -- who worked in that coffee bar or anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know about that. I really don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now, Her Honour Judge Diarra mentioned -- raised the issue of the street. Do you know if the streets on the east -- in the east part of the Mostar changed their names or did they keep their old names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know -- believe me, as far as I know, the part of the city in which I move still has the old names, and there is -- this is yet another example, and a very little one [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Are you then claiming that on the -- in East Mostar, not one street changed its name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I cannot really affirm that, because I do not move throughout that eastern part. I move in that part where I live and work, and that part -- in that part, all the streets have kept their old names.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Petar Drapsina was a communist revolutionary, one of the leaders of the communist movement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose so, seeing that the street was named after him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And are you surprised that the names of the streets were changed in those cases where streets were named after communist leaders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't know. I don't know. I don't think so, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Judge Clark?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Just arising out of those responses, we've heard a lot during this case about a coffee bar, and I'm at sea. The name of this coffee bar, Mr. Kovacevic's coffee bar, did it have a name on the front of it, besides the owner's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Garo, Garo Kovacevic. What the coffee bar was called, I don't know. I just know where it is. But I don't know really, because I never frequented coffee bars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can you tell me the old address - I don't know if the name has been changed - but the street on which this coffee bar was to be found?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't ask me about the street itself, but the neighbourhood is called Strelcevina. Just like my neighbourhood was called Dum, that neighbourhood was called Strelcevina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I'll have to look at the map. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for helping us, for giving your evidence. We all wish you good luck. The usher will show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender? Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, only the marked version of P11.18, whatever that next dash is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: 7, yes, P11.18/7. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections, and I would also like to tender the same exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. This map is admitted into evidence. I believe we should give it a double number on it. Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. Naletilic has no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you. Well, Mr. Scott, how about your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and again, so we will take the next witness -- next Bosniak witness, and Mr. Bos will be handling the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have five minutes to break. Mr. Bos, will you please brief us on the relevance of the testimony of that witness to the indictment, as well as whether there is any protective measures you will be requesting?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can do that. This witness has requested similar protective measures as the previous witness, so face and voice distortion. Well, it's fortunately all set up so I don't think that's too much of a difficulty. And the evidence of this witness is relevant to the following paragraphs in the indictment: the background, paragraphs 10 and 11; general allegations, paragraphs 18, 19, 20 and 21; count 1, paragraphs 26, 27, 28, 30, 32, and 34(a) and (b); counts 2 to 5, paragraphs 35 through 38, and paragraph 40; counts 9 to 12, paragraphs 45, 49 and 50; and counts 13 to 17, paragraphs 51 and 52.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections to the protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: None, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So your request is granted. Did you prepare a piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes, I have it right here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. What's the pseudonym for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: The pseudonym will be Witness XX. So I'll hand over the sheet now to the registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We will resume at 10 past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
